name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.23.0 (released 2026-05-18) is the latest release, adding per-visitor topic creation rate limiting to mitigate topic enumeration/squatting attacks and patching a security issue (GHSA-j8hr-p342-xrmh) in the web app's file preview. Recent prior releases (v2.19.0–v2.22.0) introduced PostgreSQL read replica support, S3-compatible attachment storage, verified email recipients, and several security/bug fixes. The project is actively maintained with frequent releases and self-hosting improvements. Full release notes are available at https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL 2.0 (client) — dual-licensed; see repository for details
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2026 with regular bug fixes and new features
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — access tokens, per-user permissions, and access control lists are supported
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted cloud version

breaking_excerpts: v2.20.0: ntfy will take full control over the attachment directory or S3 bucket — files matching the message ID format with no DB entries will be deleted. Do not reuse the attachment-cache-dir for anything else.
v2.21.0: smtp-sender-verify flag introduced requiring email address verification before sending email notifications; ntfy.sh suspended AWS SES due to unsolicited email abuse.
v2.23.0: stacktrace-js, stacktrace-gps, humanize-duration, and js-base64 removed from the web app, reducing the dependency footprint.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is an open-source notification aggregator supporting 80+ services but is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server with persistent subscriptions.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides rich cross-device notification mirroring and file sharing but is a proprietary cloud service with a limited free tier and no self-hosting.

alternatives.name: Ntfy (self-hosted) vs. Bark
alternatives.review: Bark is a lightweight self-hosted iOS-only push notification tool that is simpler to deploy than ntfy but lacks Android support and multi-subscriber pub-sub topics.
